sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].

FY2019 was the break: operating income fell 58.9% [D97] on an $8.3 billion asset impairment charge [X112], which the FY2020 filing attributes to Shave Care goodwill and Gillette intangible write-downs [P62].
FY2020 reversed it, with operating income up 186.2% [D148] as $8.3 billion of the increase came from the base-period Shave Care charge [P71].
Since then the trend is steady rather than cyclical: revenue grew 2.0% a year over FY2023..FY2026 [D664] and operating income 2.9% [D666].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue in FY2026 [D541], contributing 0.8pp of the 3.3% revenue growth [D543][D457].
That segment's 2.4% growth [D542] came from favorable foreign exchange of 1% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume unchanged [P12].
Beauty contributed more of the latest year's growth at 1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D603][D602], while Baby, Feminine & Family Care added only 0.2pp [D564].
The FY2026 top line rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Profit did not keep pace: operating income fell 3.4% [D458] against 3.3% revenue growth [D457], and diluted EPS grew 1.7% [D461] as the share count fell 1.3% [D476].
Operating margin was 22.7% in FY2026 [F30], just above the 22.1% window median [D648] and well below the 24.3% FY2025 high [D647].
The 1.6pp decline [D470] came from a 1.0pp cost-of-revenue drag and a 0.6pp SG&A drag [D483][D485], as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and SG&A rose on marketing [P25].
The largest move in the window was FY2019's 11.9pp drop [D109], almost entirely the 12.1pp residual from the impairment charge [D125].
Net margin fell only 0.5pp to 18.4% [F50][D471] because other non-operating income rose $922 million to $1.1 billion [X108][P24], partly offset by the tax rate rising to 20.8% [D443][P23].
The company sits at the 80th percentile of its five staples peers on operating margin, whose median is 14.3% [D668][D669].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income [F80][F40][D444], against a 1.25x window median [D683], and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x [F100][D445].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as net earnings plus non-cash items generated about $19.5 billion, while inventory consumed $641 million on higher safety stock [P3].
Free cash flow margin was 17.4% [D441], near the 17.2% window median [D654], and capex at 5.1% of revenue [D440] ran 1.40x D&A [D446].
Investing cash use rose to $4.6 billion on capital expenditures and hedge settlements, partly offset by Glad joint-venture proceeds [P2][F110].
The company carries net debt of $24.2 billion [D450], or 27.8% of revenue [D451], better than the three-peer median net debt of 32.3% of revenue [D695] at the 67th percentile [D694].
Liquidity is thin: cash of $9.9 billion [F140] against $34.1 billion of total debt [D449], and the current ratio is 0.68x [F180], below the 0.72x window median [D663].
Free cash flow funded $15.3 billion of buybacks and dividends, 100.7% of it [D452][D453], with $5.0 billion repurchased [X134] and $10.2 billion paid out [X144].
The diluted share count fell 1.3% [D476], and return on average equity of 30.1% [D456] trails the six-peer median of 44.4% [D681].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x every year of the window, at 0.68x in FY2026 [F180], so the negative working capital of $12.5 billion [F170] is structural rather than new.
Payout exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 and FY2026, at 116.6% and 100.7% [D402][D453], leaving little room if free cash flow dips toward its 14.4% margin low [D652].
Days inventory outstanding has climbed from 52 days in FY2017 to 69 days in FY2026 [D21][D455], with FY2026 inventory growth of 8.2% [D480] outpacing revenue growth of 3.3% [D457].
Operating margin: a print below the 22.1% window median [D648] in the FY2027 10-K would confirm the FY2026 cost pressure, while a return above the 24.3% FY2025 high [D647] would reverse it.
Free cash flow: a margin below the 14.4% window low [D652] would put the 100.7% payout ratio [D453] under strain.
Inventory: days outstanding above the FY2026 level of 69 days [D455] would extend the safety-stock build cited in the FY2026 filing [P3].
